name: crew
description: Makes the main session the one that implements, with three optional helper subagents: planner and challenger on Opus, digger on Haiku, all at high effort. The planner plans complex work, the challenger questions a decision when an independent view adds value, and the digger investigates code, git history, docs and the web; each changes files only when requested and none delegates, and no task requires one. With the jevKey option set (a TypeSafe key), Jev sizes only each helper call's effort, between medium and high; models stay at role defaults or fixed twin ids, and any Jev request or config failure requests the role default unless the agent has already sent its first step; that sends a redacted, truncated prompt to api.typesafe.ai. Each helper has a fixed-model crew:<role>-codex twin (planner and challenger on gpt-6-astra, digger on gpt-6-luna): behind a gateway other than Anthropic's API as ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, or with the codexLogin option on your Codex CLI login, where, with the crew Codex helper installed and running, all three twins run in codex app-server's workspace-write sandbox with network access and Context7 and CodeGraph as fixed MCP tools; without a ready helper a twin needs a gateway. In the codex crew mode (the mode option, or /crew-mode for one session), a plain crew:<role> call runs on its registered twin, so its work goes to OpenAI. /crew-hud opens a pane with each plan as a tree and running helper activity.

jevKey.title: Jev API key (TypeSafe)
jevKey.description: Setting this key turns Jev routing on; leaving it empty turns it off. With a key, Jev (TypeSafe) sizes only the effort of each eligible crew:* Agent call, between medium and high; models stay at role defaults or fixed twin ids. Any Jev request or config failure requests the role default (high) unless the agent has already sent its first step. The choice shows in the task's description. The call's description and its prompt (secrets and paths removed, cut to 4000 characters) are sent to api.typesafe.ai. Only the codex crew mode (the mode option or /crew-mode) may move a call to its role's Codex twin, even without this key, and a base-role call that names a model keeps it. The key is sent only in the Authorization header and is never logged or stored by the plugin. A repository's own settings cannot supply it.

mode.title: Crew mode
mode.description: The mode every session starts in. claude: crew:<role> calls run on Claude. codex: a plain crew:<role> call runs on the role's registered crew:<role>-codex twin, so its work goes to OpenAI; a role without a registered twin stays on Claude, and a call that names a model, a fork, a teammate, a workflow agent or a twin named by the lead is never moved. /crew-mode switches the running session without changing this option. A repository's own settings cannot start it in codex.

codexLogin.title: Codex twins on your Codex login (experimental)
codexLogin.description: Runs the Codex twins on your ChatGPT Codex login through the crew Codex helper (plugins/crew/helper/install.sh), with no gateway. When the helper is ready, planner, challenger and digger run in codex app-server's workspace-write sandbox: the repository and temporary directories are writable, commands have network access, and files change only when requested. Crew reads no token; the helper uses the Codex CLI login. Context7 sends library names and questions to mcp.context7.com anonymously, and CodeGraph is also available. Without a ready helper, a twin needs a gateway. A repository's own settings cannot turn this option on. Off by default.
